title: Framer Pricing 2026: Plans, Limits and What You Pay
summary: Framer pricing plans limit projects, exports and collaborators differently. Identify which constraint becomes binding before price matters.
body_markdown:
## Activepieces for Framer form and CMS automation


Nobody should buy Activepieces as a Framer alternative.


It earns a place only when Framer form submissions or content have to reach a CRM, Slack or a spreadsheet that Framer's own integrations don't cover, and its 746 integrations, roughly 60% of them community-contributed, are where that gap closes.


If your form already lands where you need it, this line item is zero and should stay off the books.


### What a form-to-spreadsheet workflow looks like


It does one narrow job: take the payload a Framer form sends, run it through a few steps, and write the result somewhere else. The example below is a "CV Scanning" flow, which isn't a Framer flow, but the shape is the same.


It starts with a web form trigger labeled "Human Input". A Google Sheets step inserts a row, a step extracts text from the attached PDF, a text-AI step summarizes it, and a second Sheets step updates the row with the summary.


With the trigger's panel open, it shows a published form URL, a draft form URL, and a warning about the "Wait for Response" setting.


That warning matters for you. If the flow waits for a response, the visitor's submission is held until the steps finish. A Framer form that should simply confirm receipt would be better off not waiting.


### Counting submissions instead of pages


Swap the web form trigger for a webhook that Framer posts to. The remaining steps are the same kind of work: append a row, notify a channel, create a CRM contact.


Each of those is a step, but the automation platform meters the run, not the step. So the unit to count isn't your Framer pages or CMS items but the number of submissions per month.


That's the number to carry into the pricing page.


For this one job, a Framer form feeding a spreadsheet, Slack and a CRM, each submission is one run and so 1 credit however many steps it has:[Activepieces' Free plan](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) includes 1,000 credits a month, Plus is $20 a month for 10,000, and either sits entirely outside your Framer plan.


Activepieces is the better fit for anyone whose Framer form submissions or content must reach a CRM, Slack or a spreadsheet that Framer's own integrations don't cover, judged on how the bill scales as the automation grows.


Its pricing page charges 1 credit per flow run regardless of how many steps sit inside it, while Zapier bills per task and Make per module, so a form flow that adds a lookup, a formatting step and a write-out costs the same as one that only writes.


If your form already lands where you need it, none of this applies and the line item should stay at zero.
